title: GPU memory budget reconciliation: proactive KV prefetch windows and elastic activation slack
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As mixed workloads run through continuous batching, transient KV cache pressure and activation spikes cause conservative static headroom allocations that reduce overall GPU utilization. We need an approach that reconciles long-lived weight occupancy, KV residency, and per-request activation slack so that we maintain tail-latency SLOs while increasing usable headroom for bursty tenants.

Goals:
- Reduce average reserved headroom by 20% on 80% of serving pods without increasing 99th-percentile latency beyond SLO.
- Provide an adaptive prefetch window for KV entries that shrinks during high activation pressure and expands during steady-state low pressure.
- Produce transparent accounting (ledger) for weight/KV/activation usage per-tenant to enable predictable billing and autoscale decisions.

Proposal (high level):
1) Memory Reconciliation Ledger: introduce a lightweight ledger per-GPU that tracks three tracked curves: weight residency (static), KV working set (time-decayed), and activation transient envelope (p99-10s rolling). The ledger exposes a single conservative headroom value computed as: total_free = gpu_capacity - weight_resident - max(kv_window, activation_envelope * alpha). alpha is a tunable slack multiplier.
2) Proactive KV Prefetch Windows: maintain an adaptive KV prefetch window size (in bytes and entry-count) driven by recent access locality and the ledger headroom. When headroom drops below a threshold, prefetch window is curtailed aggressively and prefetches are rate-limited to avoid eviction churn.
3) Elastic Activation Slack: when the ledger detects repeated low tail-latency (margin > margin_target) the runtime permits temporary expansion of activation slack for in-flight batches (speculative slack). If memory reclaim signals trigger, slack is revoked with prioritized eviction of non-critical KV entries (LRU with tenant-priority bias).
4) Accounting + Telemetry: expose per-tenant metrics for weight, kv_resident, mv_activation_peak, headroom_fraction, and headroom_reconciled_reason (kv-limited | activation-limited | weight-limited).

Design decisions & tradeoffs:
- Using a time-decayed KV working set avoids overreacting to single-request spikes but risks underestimating tail-heavy workloads. We'll tune decay half-life per workload class.
- Prefetch throttling will improve stability but may reduce model cold-start quality for very large context reuse patterns; mitigation: keep a tiny prioritized prefetch budget for recently active sessions.
- Eviction bias prefers KV entries from lower-tier tenants to protect enterprise SLAs; requires policy config and audit logging.

Implementation plan (milestones):
A. Prototype ledger + simple precedence logic (alpha tunable) in runtime local memory accounting (week 1-2).
B. Instrument metrics and a synthetic workload harness to reproduce KV+activation contention (week 3).
C. Implement adaptive prefetch window, integrate with KV fetcher and eviction policy (week 4-6).
D. Add activation slack gating and emergency revoke path with prioritized KV eviction (week 6-8).
E. Canary on Dedicated capacity pool with monitoring dashboards and automated rollback policy (week 9-10).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for ledger math and prefetch budget transitions.
- Stress tests with mixed short-chat, long-context, and embedding workloads; measure headroom, throughput, and P50/P95/P99 latency.
- Failure injection: delayed KV fetch, forced activation spikes, and GPU OOM simulation to verify revoke path and graceful degradation.

Monitoring & Alerts:
Create dashboards with: headroom_fraction over time, kv_prefetch_window, activation_envelope, reclaim_events, eviction_rates by tenant. Alerting rules: headroom_fraction < 0.08 sustained for 30s; reclaim_events > 5/min; eviction_rate rise > 200% relative to baseline.

Rollout strategy:
- Start with internal dev cluster: enable ledger read-only mode to observe reconciled headroom without altering prefetch behavior.
- Flip to reactive mode (throttling only) for low-risk tenants.
- Gradually enable speculative slack for non-SLA tiers, then enterprise with opt-in and audit.

Open questions / risks:
- How to select alpha and decay half-life defaults across diverse tenant profiles? Propose starting with adaptive defaults based on historical KV locality.
- Billing and tenant accounting model complexity if headroom fluctuates frequently — may need smoothing windows for cost attribution.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (drive): https://drive.redwood.example/runtime/memory-ledger-design (placeholder)
- Workload harness repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426
- Spike notebook with synthetic runs: https://notebooks.redwood.example/kv-activation-sim

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary shows >=15% improvement in average usable headroom on target pools with no P99 latency regression beyond 3% and no increase in OOM events over baseline.
- Telemetry surfaces headroom_reconciled_reason and reclaim events with tenant attribution.
